related_questions.question: How long do I have to wait to take a COVID test after exposure?
related_questions.snippet: If you were exposed to someone who has COVID-19 and you do not have symptoms, wait at least 5 full days after your exposure before testing. If you test too early, you may have an inaccurate result. If you are in certain high-risk settings, you may need to test as part of a screening testing program.

related_questions.question: When is the best time to take a COVID test at home?
related_questions.snippet: All COVID-19 tests can only give results that amount to a snapshot in time. That's why it makes sense to wait to take a test either until you have symptoms or until about five days after you've been exposed to someone who has tested positive for COVID-19. Taking a test immediately after exposure doesn't do much good.
